study_identification_part.si_4_title: Extreme deviations from the normative model reveal cortical heterogeneity and associations with negative symptom severity in first-episode psychosis from the OPTiMiSE and GAP studies

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used a pre-trained multi-site reference normative model (n=37,126 healthy participants across 79 scanners, age range 6-100 years; Kia et al. 2022). Clinical data were drawn from the GAP (Genetics and Psychosis) study and the OPTiMiSE (Optimization of Treatment and Management of Schizophrenia in Europe) multi-site clinical trial. An additional ATLAS control sample was incorporated into the GAP dataset to supplement older age ranges.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We used a pre-estimated multi-site reference normative model predicting cortical thickness from age. This model was built from healthy participant data (n = 37,126) across 79 scanners with good coverage through adolescence to late life"; "We included data from two large samples of individuals who were recruited and assessed at the time of their first presentation to services in the Genetics and Psychosis (GAP) study, and the Optimization of Treatment and Management of Schizophrenia in Europe (OPTiMiSE) study."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Worker2023.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modelling and statistical analysis, L74-L75; Methods / Participants, L42-L43

answer.None (Pre-Trained NM): pre-trained reference normative model of cortical thickness (n=37,126)

answer.GAP: clinical sample for model adaptation (controls) and testing (patients and remaining controls); adaptation used ATLAS control data (~124 controls), remaining controls and 123 FEP patients used as test sample

answer.OPTiMiSE: clinical sample for model adaptation (50% controls per site) and testing (remaining controls and 172 FEP patients)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The pre-trained normative model provided the reference distribution. GAP and OPTiMiSE control participants were split: a portion was used for adaptation of the normative model to the new sites (total 199 adaptation controls), and the remaining 149 controls plus 295 FEP patients formed the test sample for estimating deviations and subsequent statistical analysis.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "We used a pre-estimated multi-site reference normative model predicting cortical thickness from age."; "the parameters of this reference normative model were adapted to the new sites with 50% of control participant data from each clinical site from the OPTiMiSE sample"; "the ATLAS data was selected as the adaptation set, which is slightly over 50% of available control data. For both samples, the remaining control participant and patient data were used as test samples for estimating deviations from the normative range."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Worker2023.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modelling and statistical analysis, L74-L77

model-1.model-name: pre-trained cortical thickness normative model (Kia et al. 2022) adapted to GAP and OPTiMiSE sites

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The pre-trained reference normative model was built from 37,126 healthy participants. The exact train/test split of the original reference model is not reported in this paper. For site adaptation in this study, 199 controls were used (adaptation set), and 149 controls remained for the test set. Total controls in this study: 348.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "This model was built from healthy participant data (n = 37,126) across 79 scanners"; "199 control participant brain scans were used for adaptation of the normative reference model (mean [SD] age, 35 [16.3] years; 87 [44%] male), resulting in a test sample consisting of the 295 FEP patients and 149 control participants"
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Worker2023.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modelling and statistical analysis, L74; Results, L109

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The pre-trained reference normative model (n=37,126) had an age range of 6-100 years. Mean/SD/median of the reference model population are not reported in this paper. For the adaptation controls used in this study: mean age 35, SD 16.3 years. For the test controls: mean age 26, SD 6.7 years. These are site-adaptation and test data, not the full normative model training data.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "This model was built from healthy participant data (n = 37,126) across 79 scanners with good coverage through adolescence to late life"; "in order to maximise the coverage over the lifespan"; "199 control participant brain scans were used for adaptation of the normative reference model (mean [SD] age, 35 [16.3] years; 87 [44%] male)"
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.location: Worker2023.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modelling and statistical analysis, L74; Introduction, L35; Results, L109

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex breakdown of the 37,126 healthy participants in the pre-trained reference normative model is not reported in this paper. For the adaptation controls in this study (n=199): 87 (44%) male, 112 (56%) female (inferred: 199-87=112). For the test controls (n=149): 60 (40%) male, 89 (60%) female (inferred: 149-60=89). Sex was accounted for in the model as a batch effect.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Participant sex and scanner site have been accounted for in the model by inclusion as batch effects"; "199 control participant brain scans were used for adaptation of the normative reference model (mean [SD] age, 35 [16.3] years; 87 [44%] male)"
